# Copilot Instructions

Spring Boot 4.1 / Java 21 / Thymeleaf web front end for Companies House payments. It holds no payment data itself: it calls the Payments API through the CH `sdk-manager-java` and then redirects the user to the external payment provider.

**Type:** java-web

## Build, test, run

- Build: `mvn package -DskipTests=true` (or `make build`, which also sets the version and copies the jar to the repo root)
- All tests: `mvn test` (`make test` runs `mvn clean` first). Tests use JUnit 5 and Mockito via `spring-boot-starter-test`, and JaCoCo is configured in the pom.
- Single test class: `mvn test -Dtest=PaymentSummaryControllerTests`
- Single test method: `mvn test -Dtest=PaymentSummaryControllerTests#methodName`
- Run locally through `chs-dev` in docker-chs-development, for example `chs-dev modules enable orders`, `chs-dev development enable payments-web`, then `chs-dev up`. There is no jib; the ECS image comes from `ecs-image-build/Dockerfile`.
- No lint step is configured in this repo.
- Required env vars are in `application.properties`: `CHS_URL`, `DEVELOPER_URL`, `CHS_MONITOR_GUI_URL`, `CDN_HOST`, `PIWIK_URL`, `PIWIK_SITE_ID` and `CHS_PAYMENT_PRIVILEGE_API_KEY`. OpenTelemetry export is controlled by `OTEL_LOG_ENABLED` (default false) and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`. The README also lists `PAYMENTS_WEB_PORT` and `HUMAN_LOG`.

## Architecture

Package root: `uk.gov.companieshouse.web.payments`. The layers are controller → service → `ApiClientService` (SDK) → Payments API. Services and transformers are interface + `impl/` pairs.

- **`PaymentSummaryController`** is the only controller. It is mapped to both `/payments/{paymentId}/pay` and `/payments/{paymentId}/pay/api-key`. The request URI containing `api-key` sets an `isAPIKey` flag that is passed through `PaymentService` and `ExternalPaymentService`. The flag selects the SDK client that uses the privileged key (`CHS_PAYMENT_PRIVILEGE_API_KEY`) instead of the user's session OAuth. Any new service call must keep this flag and client selection.
- **Flow:**
  1. GET fetches the payment.
  2. If the payment is already paid, it returns the error view.
  3. If there is one payment method, it shows the summary page.
  4. If there are several methods, it shows `paymentMethodChoice`.
  5. POST patches the chosen method through the private API (`/private/payments/{id}`).
  6. POST then creates the external payment and redirects to the provider URL.
  - The `?summary=false` query parameter skips the screens, but only when there is exactly one method. Otherwise it returns the error view.
- **Models and transformers:** SDK `PaymentApi` objects are converted to web models (`PaymentSummary`, `Payment`) by the `transformer` package. Do not pass SDK models into templates.
- **`ServiceException`** is the only checked exception from services. Controllers catch it, log it with `LOGGER.errorRequest(request, ...)` and return `ERROR_VIEW` ("error"). They do not rethrow it.
- **Security (`WebSecurity`)** has two filter chains:
  1. Order 1 covers `/payments-web/healthcheck` and `/payments/*/pay/api-key`. It uses API-style CSRF mitigation and no user session auth.
  2. Order 2 covers `/**`. It uses web CSRF mitigation and `HijackFilter` and `UserAuthFilter` from the CH web security library.
  - New endpoints must be placed in the right chain.
- **Interceptors** are registered in `PaymentsWebApplication`: `LoggingInterceptor` and `UserDetailsInterceptor`.
- **Healthcheck** is at `/payments-web/healthcheck` (actuator, with only `health` exposed).
- **Templates** are in `src/main/resources/templates`: layouts, fragments and `payments/`. Every controller must implement `getTemplateName()` from `BaseController`, which exposes it to the layout as the `templateName` model attribute.

## Dependency management

- `pom.xml` imports `ch-dependency-bom` and `ch-test-bom` (shared `ch-boms.version`) before `spring-boot-dependencies`, so CH-approved versions win. Don't add version pins the BOMs already manage.
- `common-web-java` looks unused in the code but supplies runtime templates (`error.html`, layouts, fragments) and locale messages. Don't remove it.
- `OpenTelemetryAppenderInitializer` installs the logback OTel appender only when `management.opentelemetry.enabled=true`.

## Deployment

The `terraform/` and `ecs-image-build/` directories define the AWS ECS deployment (Concourse pipeline). The `version` file and the `make package` target are used by that pipeline. Don't edit the `*.jar` and `*.zip` files in the repo root by hand.

# CHS Java Development Standards

These standards apply to **all** Companies House Java services and libraries
regardless of service type. Service-type-specific standards (`java-api.md`,
`java-web.md`, `java-library.md`) supplement this file — read this first.

**Authoritative style reference:** [`companieshouse/styleguides` — Java](https://github.com/companieshouse/styleguides/blob/main/standards/java.md)
(based on Google Java Style Guide with CH modifications: 4-space indent,
130-char line length, K&R braces). All code must also pass the
[CH Checkstyle configuration](https://github.com/companieshouse/java-checkstyle-config).

---

## 1. Code Style

> **[CH Required]** All Java code must pass the [CH Checkstyle configuration](https://github.com/companieshouse/java-checkstyle-config). The CI pipeline enforces this.
>
> **[CH Required]** No Lombok. Write explicit constructors, getters, and setters. Source: [CH Java styleguide](https://github.com/companieshouse/styleguides/blob/main/standards/java.md)
>
> **[CH Required]** Constructor injection only — never `@Autowired` on fields or setters. Source: [CH Java styleguide](https://github.com/companieshouse/styleguides/blob/main/standards/java.md)

### General
- Use `var` for local variables where the type is obvious from the right-hand
  side (Java 17+); do not use it when the type aids readability
- `static final` constants over inline literals; group related constants in a
  dedicated `Constants` class (or `JsonConstants` for JSON field names)
- Comments only where the code genuinely needs clarification; self-explanatory
  code needs no comment
- Always use `@Override` when overriding methods
- Javadoc required on all public classes and public/protected members (unless
  self-evident like `getId()`); `@param`, `@return`, `@throws` in that order

### Naming
- Method and variable names must be self-documenting — avoid abbreviations
  and single-letter names outside loop counters
- Non-obvious design decisions must have a comment explaining **why**, not what
- Keep methods short and focused — a method that needs a comment to explain
  its own structure should be split

### Exception handling
- Never swallow exceptions silently — always log with full context and
  either rethrow or return an appropriate error response
- Include the full exception object in error log calls, not just `e.getMessage()`
- When wrapping a caught exception in a custom type, always pass the original as
  the cause — `throw new MyException("message", e)` — never construct from
  `e.getMessage()` alone; the stack trace is otherwise silently discarded,
  making production diagnosis much harder

---

## 2. Logging

> **[CH Required]** Use the Companies House structured logger throughout. Do not use `System.out.println` or other ad-hoc logging. Source: CH convention.
>
> **[CH Required]** PII must never appear in logs at any level. Log IDs (UUIDs, userIds, company numbers), never values (names, emails, document details). Source: [Secure SDLC](https://companieshouse.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/973242435)

Use `LoggerFactory.getLogger(ApplicationNamespace.APPLICATION_NAMESPACE)` and always pass a `Map<String, Object>` context — never concatenate values into the message string.

| Level | When to use |
|---|---|
| `DEBUG` | Detailed trace. Suppressed in production. |
| `INFO` | Significant business events. |
| `WARN` | Recoverable issues; unexpected but handled state. |
| `ERROR` | Exceptions — always include the full exception object, never just `e.getMessage()`. |

---

## 3. Testing

### Framework
- JUnit 5 only (`org.junit.jupiter.*`) — never add or use JUnit 4 (`org.junit.*`)
- `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)` with `@Mock` and `@InjectMocks`
- `assertThrows` from `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`, not JUnit 4 `Assert`
- Test class names mirror the class under test with a `Test` suffix

### Quality
- Test names describe expected behaviour, not implementation: prefer
  `shouldReturn404WhenCompanyNotFound` over `testGetCompany`
- Mock external service calls with Mockito; never rely on live endpoints
- Tests must fail before the implementation exists — do not write tests that
  pass against a stub

---

## 4. Maven and Dependencies

### BOM imports

> **[CH Required]** All CHS Java services must import `ch-dependency-bom` and
> `ch-test-bom` in `<dependencyManagement>`. Do not redeclare version numbers
> for any dependency managed by those BOMs. Source: CH Maven convention.

### Dependency discipline
- If the service code directly imports or uses a class from a library, that
  library must be declared explicitly in `<dependencies>` — do not rely on
  transitive dependencies
- Do not add a dependency to `pom.xml` that is never imported in the codebase
- Keep `<dependencyManagement>` and `<dependencies>` free of duplicates
- Test-scoped dependencies must use `<scope>test</scope>`
- Remove unused dependencies

### Checking dependency versions
CH libraries are published to Artifactory at `https://chartifacts.jfrog.io` — always check here first for CH library versions, not Maven Central. Credentials are in `~/.m2/settings.xml`. Running `mvn dependency:tree` locally resolves from Artifactory automatically.

### Running OWASP dependency-check locally (`depcheck`)
When a Maven repo's CI dependency-check fails on a CVE, it can be reproduced
locally with the `depcheck` tool from
[`companieshouse/dependency-check-suppressions`](https://github.com/companieshouse/dependency-check-suppressions)
rather than guessing at fixes from the CVE description alone. This runs the
exact same containerised OWASP dependency-check used in CI, including the
centralised suppressions.

Before offering to run it, ask the user: **"Do you have `depcheck` installed
locally?"** If yes, just run it — do not walk them through installation
first.

```bash
# From the repo under test:
depcheck --
```

If `depcheck` is not on PATH, the one-time setup is documented at
`companieshouse/dependency-check-suppressions` (clone it, set
`DEPENDENCY_CHECK_SUPPRESSIONS_HOME`, add the `depcheck` alias) — see that
repo's README rather than re-deriving the steps.

Requires Docker running and Docker authenticated against the CH ECR registry
(session may need `aws sso login` + `aws ecr get-login-password | docker
login` first if the pull fails with an auth error).

After fixing (e.g. bumping a `<*.version>` property in `pom.xml`), re-run
`depcheck --` to confirm `BUILD SUCCESS` before considering the CVE resolved.
Note: this only reflects the **current local working tree** — it is not the
same as, and can catch CVEs sooner than, whatever SBOM snapshot is recorded
in Dependency Track for a previously published release.

---

## 5. Local Development

CHS Java services run in the Docker CHS development environment (`docker-chs-development`) via `chs-dev`. Run tests directly with `./mvnw test`. Environment variables go in `.env` at the repo root (gitignored).

# CHS Java Web Service Standards

These standards apply to Companies House Java web services (Spring Boot +
Spring MVC + Thymeleaf). They supplement `core.md` and the common Java
standards in `java.md` — read both of those first.

**Authoritative style reference:** [`companieshouse/styleguides` — Java](https://github.com/companieshouse/styleguides/blob/main/standards/java.md)
and [CH Checkstyle configuration](https://github.com/companieshouse/java-checkstyle-config).

The key distinction from a Java API: this service renders HTML pages for
browsers, not JSON for API consumers. Controllers return view names or
redirects, not `ResponseEntity`.

---

## 1. Technology Stack

| Concern | Library |
|---|---|
| Framework | Spring Boot + Spring MVC |
| Templating | Thymeleaf |
| UI components | GOV.UK Frontend (via Thymeleaf fragments or Webjars) |
| Session | `java-session-handler` (`@companieshouse/java-session-handler`) |
| Logging | CH structured logging (`structured-logging`) |
| Security | Spring Security + `web-security-java` |
| Testing | JUnit 5 + Mockito + MockMvc |

---

## 2. Controllers

- Annotate with `@Controller` (not `@RestController` — this renders views)
- Return a `String` (view name) or `ModelAndView` from handler methods
- Use `RedirectAttributes` for flash messages across redirects

> **[CH Required]** Post-Redirect-Get pattern is mandatory for all form submissions — always redirect after a successful POST to prevent duplicate submission on browser refresh.

- Delegate all business logic to service classes — controllers handle only
  request binding, validation, model population, and view selection

---

## 3. Thymeleaf Templates

- Use GOV.UK Frontend components — do not invent custom UI patterns
- Keep templates logic-free — conditional logic belongs in the controller
  or a `@ControllerAdvice` model attribute, not in templates
- Use Thymeleaf fragments for shared components (header, footer, error summary)
- Every form input must have an associated `<label>` and a GOV.UK error
  message component wired to binding result errors using `aria-describedby`
- User-visible strings go in message property files (`messages.properties`,
  `messages_cy.properties`) — never hardcode in templates or controllers

---

## 4. Session Handling

Use the CHS `java-session-handler` library for all session operations.

- Never store PII in the session beyond what is strictly necessary for the
  current user journey step
- Clear journey-specific session data when the journey completes
- Session data must be serialisable — use simple types and POJOs

---

## 5. Security

### Required for all services
- Spring Security configured via `web-security-java`
- CSRF protection enabled on all state-changing routes (POST/PUT/DELETE)
- Thymeleaf CSRF integration: include `th:action` on all forms (automatically
  includes the CSRF token)
- Content Security Policy (CSP) headers configured
- Authentication enforced via CHS OAuth2 / sign-in service

### Input validation
- Use Bean Validation (`@Valid`, `@NotBlank`, `@Size` etc.) on form model objects
- Custom validators for business rules that cannot be expressed with standard annotations
- Validate at the controller boundary — never trust form input downstream

---

## 6. Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA is the required standard for CHS public-facing services (legal
obligation under the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018).
Welsh language support is required under the Welsh Language Act 2011.

Full standards, tooling requirements, Welsh language implementation details,
and audit gate requirements are in `instructions/accessibility.md`.

---

## 7. Testing

Use MockMvc for controller tests (`@WebMvcTest`). Mock service dependencies with `@MockBean`.

### Coverage expectations
- Every GET route: renders expected view, populates model correctly
- Every POST route: happy path redirect, validation failure re-render, CSRF rejection (`with(csrf())`)
- Every authentication-required route: unauthenticated request redirects to sign-in
- Service layer: full unit test coverage

---

## 7. Error Handling

- Centralise exception handling in a shared abstract base controller or a
  `@ControllerAdvice` class using `@ExceptionHandler` methods — do not add
  `try/catch` blocks in individual controllers that return error views
- **Never call `response.sendError()`** — it bypasses Spring's
  `DispatcherServlet` exception handling chain, producing inconsistent error
  pages and losing structured logging. Throw a typed exception instead and let
  the centralised handler route to the appropriate error page
- Distinguish 4xx (client/user error) from 5xx (service fault) in your
  `@ExceptionHandler` and redirect to the appropriate error page — users should
  receive a meaningful response, not a generic "something went wrong"
- The centralised handler is the single place responsible for logging and for
  ensuring no internal implementation details (stack traces, internal paths)
  reach the rendered response

---

## 8. Local Development

```bash
./mvnw test
./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=local
```

Environment variables go in `.env` or `application-local.properties` (gitignored). See `.env.example` for required variables.

# CHS Accessibility Standards

These standards apply to all Companies House user-facing web services (Java web
and Node.js web). They supplement `core.md` — read that first.

**Legal basis:** The Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications)
Accessibility Regulations 2018 require all public sector digital services to
meet WCAG 2.2 AA. Companies House also operates under the Welsh Language
Act 2011 and the Welsh Language (Wales) Measure 2011 as a public body.

**Authoritative references:**
- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) — the W3C standard
- [GOV.UK Accessibility Requirements](https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/helping-people-to-use-your-service/making-your-service-accessible-an-introduction)
- [CH Accessibility Developer Checklist](https://companieshouse.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/5404721275)

---

## 1. WCAG Standard

- **Minimum standard: WCAG 2.2 AA** for all public-facing CHS services
- WCAG 2.1 AA is the floor for internal tools — 2.2 is still the target
- GOV.UK Frontend implements WCAG-compliant patterns by design — use it;
  do not override or disable its accessible behaviours
- Accessibility is a first-class requirement, not a pre-launch checklist item

---

## 2. Developer Tooling

Run these checks before raising a PR — they are not optional:

| Tool | Where | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| **axe Linter** | VS Code / IntelliJ plugin | Static WCAG violations in templates |
| **WAVE** | Browser extension | Runtime violations, contrast, ARIA |
| **Keyboard navigation** | Manual test | All flows navigable without a mouse |
| **axe-core** | CI (where configured) | Automated regression on rendered pages |

Zero axe errors and zero WAVE errors are the baseline. Warnings should be
reviewed and either resolved or documented as accepted deviations.

---

## 3. Required Checks for Every Page/Template

### Structure
- Single `<h1>` per page; heading hierarchy is logical (no skipped levels)
- Page `<title>` is descriptive, unique, and follows the pattern
  `Page name - Service name - GOV.UK`
- Skip link to main content is present and functional
- Landmark regions are used correctly (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<header>`, `<footer>`)

### Forms
- Every input has a visible `<label>` associated by `for`/`id`
- Error messages use the GOV.UK error pattern — associated with the field
  via `aria-describedby` or the error summary pattern
- Required fields are indicated in a way that does not rely on colour alone
- Form groups use the GOV.UK `govuk-form-group--error` pattern on validation failure

### Interaction
- All interactive elements are keyboard-accessible (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space)
- Focus is never lost or trapped — visible focus indicator present at all times
- No keyboard trap exists at any point in the user journey
- Dynamic content changes (e.g. errors appearing) are announced to screen readers
  via `aria-live` regions or focus management
- Core functionality (navigation, form submission, reading content) works with
  JavaScript disabled — use progressive enhancement; avoid custom/local
  JavaScript where GOV.UK Frontend's built-in, no-JS-first behaviour already
  covers the need

### Content
- Link text is descriptive in isolation — no "click here", "read more", or bare "here"
- Colour is never the only means of conveying information (status, error, required)
- Images that convey information have descriptive `alt` text; decorative images
  have `alt=""`
- Content is readable and functional at 200% browser zoom

### ARIA
- Use native HTML semantics before reaching for ARIA — `<button>` not
  `<div role="button">`
- ARIA roles, states, and properties must be valid and used correctly
- Do not add ARIA to elements that already have implicit semantics
  (e.g. `role="heading"` on an `<h2>`)

---

## 4. Screen Reader Testing

Test with at least one screen reader before raising a PR on UI changes:

| Platform | Screen reader | Paired browser |
|---|---|---|
| macOS / iOS | VoiceOver (built-in) | Safari |
| Windows | NVDA (free) | Firefox |
| Windows | JAWS 15+ | Chrome or IE11 |
| Voice control | Dragon NaturallySpeaking 11+ | Chrome |

Test: focus order, form field announcements, error message announcements,
page title on navigation, and modal/overlay behaviour (if applicable).

---

## 5. Welsh Language

Companies House is subject to the Welsh Language Act 2011. All public-facing
web services must provide full Welsh language support.

### When Welsh is required
- All public-facing CHS web services
- All form labels, error messages, page titles, headings, and button text
- Email notifications sent to users
- Accessibility statements
- Welsh is **not** required for purely internal tools or admin interfaces

### Node.js implementation
- English strings in locale files (e.g. `locales/en/translation.json`)
- Welsh equivalents in Welsh locale files (e.g. `locales/cy/translation.json`)
- Use `@companieshouse/ch-node-utils` LocalesService for locale switching
- Language toggle must be present on every page (GOV.UK Frontend header pattern)
- Every key added to the English locale file must have a corresponding Welsh key

### Java web implementation
- English strings in `src/main/resources/messages.properties`
- Welsh strings in `src/main/resources/messages_cy.properties`
- Every key added to `messages.properties` must have a corresponding key in
  `messages_cy.properties`
- Never hardcode user-visible strings in controllers or templates

### Welsh content quality
- Do **not** use machine translation — use the approved CH translation service
- Test all flows with the language set to Welsh before raising a PR
- Verify that switching language mid-journey works correctly and that the
  session preserves the user's language preference

---

## 6. Audit Gates

> **[CH Required]** All public-facing services require an external accessibility
> audit before going live. A service must not go live without passing this audit.
> Legal obligation under the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile
> Applications) Accessibility Regulations 2018.

CH uses external auditors including AbilityNet, DAC, and Hassell Inclusion.

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Pre-Alpha/Prototype | Check GOV.UK Frontend patterns are used correctly |
| Pre-Beta | Internal accessibility check: developer checklist + WAVE + keyboard nav |
| Pre-Live | **External accessibility audit** — mandatory |
| Post-significant-change | Re-audit when primary UI is substantially changed |
| Annual | Review and update accessibility statement |

A service **must not go live** without passing an external accessibility audit.
If issues are found, they must have a documented remediation plan and timeline.

---

## 7. Accessibility Statement

Every public-facing service must publish an accessibility statement. It must:
- State the WCAG conformance level targeted (WCAG 2.2 AA)
- List any known accessibility issues with a realistic remediation timeline
- Provide contact details for users who need help or to report issues
- Be kept current — a stale statement is itself a compliance risk
- Follow the [GOV.UK model accessibility statement](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/model-accessibility-statement)
